title: Parametric Equations
lead: A parametric curve is traced by a point whose coordinates $x$ and $y$ both depend on a third variable, the parameter $t.$ This section graphs such curves with their orientation, eliminates the parameter to find an equation in $x$ and $y,$ parameterizes a curve in more than one way and follows a rolling wheel’s cycloid.
objectives: Plot a curve described by parametric equations.
Convert the parametric equations of a curve into the form $y=f(x).$
Recognize the parametric equations of basic curves, such as a line and a circle.
Recognize the parametric equations of a cycloid.
summary_html:
• Parametric equations provide a convenient way to describe a curve. A parameter can represent time or some other meaningful quantity.
  • It is often possible to eliminate the parameter in a parameterized curve to obtain a function or relation describing that curve.
  • There is always more than one way to parameterize a curve.
  • Parametric equations can describe complicated curves that are difficult or perhaps impossible to describe using rectangular coordinates.

exercises.prompt:
Sketch the curve described by the parametric equations

$$x(t)=3t+2,\;y(t)=t^{2}-1,\;-3\le t\le 2.$$

answer.hint: Make a table of values for $x(t)$ and $y(t)$ using t values from −3 to 2.

exercises.prompt:
Eliminate the parameter for the plane curve defined by the following parametric equations and describe the resulting graph.

$$x(t)=2+\frac{3}{t},\;y(t)=t-1,\;2\le t\le 6$$

answer.solution: $x=2+\frac{3}{y+1},$ or $y=-1+\frac{3}{x-2}.$ This equation describes a portion of a rectangular hyperbola centered at $(2,-1).$
answer.hint: Solve one of the equations for t and substitute into the other equation.

exercises.prompt: Find two different sets of parametric equations to represent the graph of $y=x^{2}+2x.$

answer.solution: One possibility is $x(t)=t,\;y(t)=t^{2}+2t.$ Another possibility is $x(t)=2t-3,\;y(t)={(2t-3)}^{2}+2(2t-3)=4t^{2}-8t+3.$ There are, in fact, an infinite number of possibilities.
answer.hint: Follow the steps in Example 11.3. Remember we have freedom in choosing the parameterization for $x(t).$

exercises.prompt: Show that $\begin{array}{l}x=h+r\;\cos \theta \\ y=k+r\;\sin \theta \end{array}$ represents the equation of a circle.

answer.solution: Subtract $h$ and $k$: $x-h=r\cos \theta$ and $y-k=r\sin \theta .$ Square both equations and add them; the Pythagorean identity ${\cos }^{2}\theta +{\sin }^{2}\theta =1$ eliminates the parameter: ${(x-h)}^{2}+{(y-k)}^{2}=r^{2}({\cos }^{2}\theta +{\sin }^{2}\theta )=r^{2}.$ This is the equation of a circle of radius $r$ centered at $(h,k),$ and as $\theta$ runs from $0$ to $2\pi$ the point $(x,y)$ goes once around it, counterclockwise.
